0.1 This
Institution Vegitables and Food

FOREWORD

Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards on 3 January 1974, after the draft finalized by the Fruits and Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural Products Division Council.

0.2 To ensure fuller utilization of perishable foodstuffs, such as fruits and vegetables, they should be preserved under conditions which will keep Storing them them fit for human consumption over a reasonable period. in refrigerated space ( cold storage ) is an important method of preservation. To provide guidelines for the cold storage industry in the country, a series of Indian Standard Guides, based on the corresponding IS0 It is hoped that these guides which recommendations, are being issued. describe the pre-storage treatments and optimum storage conditions for different fruits and vegetables would help the industry develop on scientific lines. 0.3 In the preparation,of this standard, assistance has been derived from the research carried out at the Central Food Technological Research Institute, Mysore, and the IS0 draft proposal on the subject.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard describes the pre-storage treatment and conditions, with or without refrigeration, for citrus fruits. 1.1.1 The
following conditions species: described in this standard shall the apply storage to the

a) Orange, b) Mandarin, c) Lime,

PRE - STORAGE TREATMENTS

3.1 Sorting and Washing - After a preliminary sorting remove leaves, trash and defective ones ( such as those that are damaged or strongly infected with Phytopthora ), fruits should be \\~tshcd, prcfernbly by spraying ( which, reduces the risk of infection ), or 1)~ \\.atcring or soaking. IS : 7192- 1974 3.3 After
fungicidal treatment, fruits may be given a wax coating to replace the natural coating of fruits which is partly or entirely removed while washing and brushing. Emulsions of vegetable wax, or paraffin An approved fungicide, such as waxes should be used for this purpose. sodium orthophenylphenate, thialendezole and benlote 50, may be mixed in the wax. The amount of wax may be increased when long keeping time is anticipated. The maximum amount of wax recommended is 140 mg per kg of fruits. 3.4 After the fungicidal treatment and wax coating, second sorting and It shall be carried out very carefully without caussizing is to tie done. ing any damage to the skin of fruits. 4.
